On Fri, Jan 15, 2027 at 10:05 AM Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Maya — looping in Legal (Karthik), Marketing (Laura) and CS (Monica) to confirm what we can commit to in the Order Form.

Thanks for the ping. A few legal points after a quick review of the proposed Order Form:

1) Publicity review window: we prefer a 30-calendar-day review for any press copy that references the customer or uses the customer's logo. Seven business days is unusually short for larger enterprise customers and could risk misrepresentation. We can be flexible if Helio agrees to a specific SLA (e.g., 5 business days for short social announcements, 30 days for press releases).

2) Reference/performance numbers: any specific metrics (uptime, latency, cost savings) must be mutually agreed and supported by telemetry or audit logs. We recommend language that requires explicit written approval for cited performance figures and prohibits extrapolation beyond the agreed dataset.

3) Logo usage: we will accept use of the Helio logo for co-marketing but request a clause limiting the appearance to "Helio Systems (customer)" and prohibiting implications of endorsement or joint venture. Also add a maximum size/placement guideline and require a logo checklist to accompany any assets.

4) Confidentiality carveout: the MSA's confidentiality section must not be interpreted as an automatic opt-in to promotional materials. Add explicit opt-in for publicity and define the review cycle, plus an exception for sharing the customer's name in a list of customers ("customer roster") unless the customer requests anonymity.

I've prepared suggested redline language; see attached (Helio_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Key snippet below for quick reference:

--- suggested publicity clause (preview) ---
"Neither party shall use the other party's name, logo, or trademarks in marketing, press releases, customer lists, or other public materials without the prior written consent of the other party. Consent requests will include the proposed materials and may not be unreasonably withheld; the responding party shall provide approval or proposed edits within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt. Approval for specific performance metrics requires supporting evidence and separate written consent."

If Helio would like a shorter turnaround for specific asset types (e.g., social posts < 3 lines), we can agree to a 5-business-day SLA in the Order Form as an exception.

Let me know if you want Legal to propose final wording for signature.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
